title: U.S. House · Texas's 34th District
area: A South Texas district covering the Rio Grande Valley, including Brownsville and McAllen.

context.text: Rep. Vicente Gonzalez Jr. is the incumbent under Texas's 2026 congressional map. Eric Flores won the Republican nomination.

priorities.text: Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus and supports an "all-the-above" energy approach.
priorities.quote: Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy and understands the importance of American energy not only to power our cars and homes, but also as a national security issue and a job creator.

priorities.text: Supports agricultural research, trade assistance, and crop insurance and disaster assistance programs for South Texas farmers and ranchers.
Says he works to lower health care costs and expand coverage, particularly for South Texas's uninsured and underinsured population.

positions.summary: In a July 2026 press release, says he will push the administration to rein in ICE and opposes what he calls hyperaggressive ICE raids, while saying he supports deporting criminals.
positions.quote: to push the Administration for commonsense solutions that keep people safe, restore a critical workforce, and rein in ICE.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services in the 2025-2026 (119th) Congress.
Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus.

priorities.text: Says he supports securing the border and law enforcement.
Says he will defend the Second Amendment and advocate for veterans and U.S. energy independence.
Says he will support President Trump's agenda.
Says he would lower the cost of living by opposing federal spending that fuels inflation and cutting red tape for families and small businesses.
priorities.quote: I'll oppose reckless federal spending that fuels inflation, fight to cut the red tape driving up costs for families and small businesses

priorities.text: Says he would work to reduce VA wait times and expand access to care for veterans.
priorities.quote: I'll fight to reduce VA wait times and expand access to care throughout our communities

priorities.text: Supports plugging and decommissioning idle oil and gas wells he says are contaminating water sources.
Supports banning fracking and stopping new fossil-fuel infrastructure, including proposed LNG export terminals on the Gulf Coast.
Lists Medicare for All, free college and trade schools, and canceling student debt among his priorities.
Says he would end forever wars and cut military spending in half.
priorities.quote: Stop wasting money on forever wars, instead invest in our people: end the American Empire, and cut military spending in half.

priorities.text: Says he rejects support from all PACs, including AIPAC.
priorities.quote: Rejects support from all PACs, including AIPAC and their allies

positions.summary: Supports banning fracking, halting new fossil-fuel infrastructure, and decarbonizing the Texas economy.
positions.quote: Let's ban fracking and stop the expansion of new fossil fuels infrastructure and projects, including proposed LNG export terminals along the Gulf coast. Decarbonize the Texas economy, and make it more resilient to global warming.

positions.summary: Supports an arms embargo and conditioning military aid to Israel.
positions.quote: Supports an arms embargo and conditioning military aid to Israel

positions.summary: Supports improving and expanding Medicare for All with no co-pays or premiums.
positions.quote: Improve and expand Medicare for All, with no co-pays or premiums, including free vision care, hearing aids, dental, and prescriptions.

priorities.text: Says immigration laws already on the books should be enforced.
priorities.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.

priorities.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, said inflation is the main problem for families and the solution is to stop federal spending.
priorities.quote: Easy. Stop the spending by the Federal Government.

priorities.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, listed schools, Social Security benefits for seniors and energy independence among his concerns.
priorities.quote: I want to be on the side of energy independence because we were once there.

statements.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.

researchNotes: Espinoza's and Royal's positions rely on their 2024 Candidate Connection survey responses, as neither has completed a 2026 survey; no newer statements were found to indicate a change in position. Espinoza's additional positions come from his campaign site (espinoza4tx.com). Eric Flores's site and press coverage give priorities but no statement squarely taking a side on the guide issues. Chris Royal's campaign site could not be found; the Libertarian Party page lists only a biography. Royal's positions rely on his 2024 Candidate Connection survey responses, as he has not completed a 2026 survey; Espinoza completed a 2026 survey. Eric Flores has not completed a Candidate Connection survey, so his biography relies on his campaign biography as reported by news outlets and Ballotpedia; his campaign site's About page could not be loaded.
